faqs.question: What flange standards does Dhruv EPC fabricate to?
faqs.answer: Plate flanges are fabricated to ASME B16.5 (NPS ½ – NPS 24) and ASME B16.47 Series A (MSS SP-44) and Series B (API 605) for large-bore flanges above NPS 24 — covering all pressure classes from ASME 150 through 2,500.

faqs.question: What types of plate flanges do you supply?
faqs.answer: Weld-neck, slip-on, blind, long-weld-neck, spectacle blinds and ring-type-joint (RTJ) flanges — all plate-cut from certified plate material, rough-bored and finish-machined to ASME dimensional and face-finish tolerances.

faqs.question: Which materials are available for plate flanges?
faqs.answer: Carbon steel (ASTM A105 equivalent), low-temperature carbon steel (A350 LF2), low alloy steels (A182 F11/F22), austenitic stainless steel (A182 F304/F316) and duplex stainless steel (A182 F51).

faqs.question: Can you fabricate spectacle blinds for line isolation?
faqs.answer: Yes — figure-8 spectacle blinds and blank-and-spacer sets are plate-cut, drilled and machined to the customer's piping class; face finish matches the connected flange standard.

faqs.question: What are equipment base frames and why machine them in-house?
faqs.answer: Sole plates, base frames and levelling pads are machined flat and parallel at the Manjusar works before dispatch — in-house machining ensures co-planarity of bearing surfaces, critical for rotating-equipment alignment and vibration performance.
